subject: Independent bounded review of BDX system-call annotations

scope.semanticReview: All 33 annotation texts reviewed against captured adapter/helper code; selected side-effect and conversion paths traced. This does not close every transitive native callback or prove whole-program reachability.

findings.before: Both +20 and +24 were described as float rate/duration.
findings.after: Field +20 is a float rate; +24 is a signed DWORD duration/count, zero replaced by one. The updater converts elapsed float with CVTTSS2SI and uses signed JGE.
findings.resolution: Author updated generator, annotation, claim and report and added four byte-checked semantic anchors. Final texts and original instructions agree.

confirmed: Fade adapters 0:31/32 set hidden R8B=1; 0:87/88 clear R8D. Duration conversion is float/2 then CVTTSS2SI. Helper doubles in ECX and converts zero-extended RCX, so negative values cannot be described as an ordinary signed duration. Zero and wrapping cases remain explicit.
Fade state 1 uses a two-pass delay before state 2. State 4 reaches native callbacks; this is not a synchronous no-callback color setter.

Timer helpers clamp countdown at zero and call native 3AABE0 with (74,0) at the captured limit path. Count-up overflow above 215999 returns before that limit test. The number 74 is not relabeled as a BDX event or time unit.

Child-VM creation uses a nonzero subset-mask match for prior-child destruction. Teardown runs the exit script through 3E1410 before the allocator virtual free. The creator has an unchecked allocation-failure path; no lifetime or safety guarantee follows from the descriptor.

Grouped flag reads retain the exact signed-shift/index formula and 65535 sentinel. Flag action records can recurse and trigger follow-up native code. Queued flag lookup retains NULL-key and unchecked-result limits.

Inventory result semantics distinguish outer policy success from actual insertion; removal paths differ by item type. Completion queries can allocate or mutate state. Resource-list presence does not establish a global I/O fence, and resource repacking can relocate/free records.

Input masks are mapped bitsets, not physical scan codes. Allocation/free use the current owner. Sound annotation retains explicit native arguments. Blend outputs are task-driven integer values, with no unsupported wall-clock guarantee.
limits: No game, script, native game function, process attachment, injection, UI operation or save mutation was performed.

The original PE reader is reused from a separate frozen registry study. Byte checks and Capstone decoding are independent of the reviewed study verifier; this is not a second independently implemented PE parser.
All listed instruction spans and recorded body/chunk bytes were checked. Full argument validity, external callbacks, allocator ownership, runtime state and concurrency remain outside this review.
No new RNG analysis or universal reachability claim. The annotation descriptions remain bounded to the captured native paths.
No unresolved blocking finding remains in this reviewed scope.
changesByReviewer: Only files in artifacts/review-bdx-system-calls-20261008. No study, product, central coverage or version edits.
